reproducedProblems: The actual old cheap dispatch gate admits a matching task published before first worker activation. No immutable activation evidence existed.

The actual old Need guard rejects metadata changes with a NULL lifecycle token but admits same-revision published_at and revision changes with empty/unrelated tokens. Proven isolated SQL boundary only; no HTTP exploit claim.
Adding profile columns changes whole-row worker AI source/hash and avatar source markers. A normal backfill also changes updated_at through its existing trigger.

implementation.firstActivation: Existing confirmed activation writer stamps FIRST_ACTIVATION once through the late profile guard.
implementation.backfill: Existing ACTIVE worker profiles receive one observed rollout threshold labelled ROLLOUT_ACTIVE_OBSERVED, never a fabricated historic activation date. DRAFT and REQUESTER profiles remain NULL.
implementation.backfillContinuity: The migration retains the ALTER lock and uses a temporary late BEFORE trigger only for an exact ACTIVE WORKER metadata-only update. It preserves old updated_at, rejects any other change, and drops itself and its helper before COMMIT. All seven existing BEFORE profile guards stay enabled.
implementation.dispatch: Only the existing cheap proactive-admission gate requires published_at > worker_dispatch_eligible_since; shared matching/Discovery and manual response eligibility stay independent.
implementation.publicationWitness: Existing CONFIRM_EDIT and narrow authorized closure returns are preserved. Any other revision change is rejected. published_at can change only for a canonical PUBLISH DRAFT-to-PUBLISHED transition.
implementation.aiAndAvatarContinuity: Existing worker AI source and the two avatar marker owners exclude only the new internal columns; all previous profile material remains in their hashes.
implementation.privacy: Existing export catalogue/snapshot and closure patch include or erase the two columns. No privacy readiness, legal policy or certificate is enabled or repinned.
implementation.runtime: Existing dispatch_tick, marketplace_tick, Cron, budget, remote wave settings and Edge workers are not changed.

New avatar claims use the same semantic hash; a real profile bio change still produces MEDIA_VERSION_CONFLICT.
Unknown or disabled BEFORE profile triggers cause fail-closed migration drift rejection.
Spoofed profile clock insert/update/erase rejected for authenticated and service-role claims; service role has no generic bypass.
